# [EP 12: Demo Day]{.flow} {.title}

## The investor is in the room

Back in Session VI she stood at a whiteboard and asked why everything here was built from scratch. Today the answer is on your screens: built by you, with the standard library, pandas, plots, git, and an agent you learned to supervise.

. . .

The rules: **7 minutes** presenting, **3 minutes** of questions, order drawn at random.

## While you watch

- Note one thing you would have done differently, and one thing you are taking for your own next project
- Questions are part of the format: specific, kind, useful

# [Your Future with AI]{.flow} {.title}

## AI and your first job

- **US:** in jobs AI can largely do, employment of 22-25-year-olds trails their peers by **19%**, through fewer hires, not layoffs [@brynjolfsson_canaries_2026]
- **Sweden:** a smaller gap of **5.5%**. Job ads fell with interest rates rather than with AI [@lodefalk_same_2026]
- **Denmark:** accountants, HR, marketing, office clerks: no effect on pay or hours above **2%** [@humlum_still_2026]

. . .

So far: [fewer junior hires]{.highlight}, no economy-wide job losses, size disputed. All three are working papers.

## What AI does to work and skill

- **BCG consultants:** with AI, **12.2%** more tasks, **25.1%** faster. On a task beyond AI's reach, **19%** less likely to be right [@dellacqua_navigating_2026-1]
- **Patent lawyers:** AI lifted the juniors' work, but judgment *without* AI grew [only for the seniors]{.highlight} (working paper) [@autor_does_2026]
- **Developers learning a new library:** **17%** lower on the quiz with AI, worst on **debugging** (preprint) [@shen_how_2026]
- At school, an AI tutor giving hints, not answers, largely removed the learning loss [@bastani_generative_2025]. Part I worked the same way

## What stays valuable

- At P&G, one person with AI [matched a team]{.highlight} without it [@dellacqua_cybernetic_2026]
- Today you showed projects built with an agent you supervised, twelve sessions after your first `print()`
- The verification boundary: usable delegation ends where your ability to **check** ends. Growing that boundary outward is your career
- Your edge, deliberately kept: **explain every line before you accept it**, and work without AI sometimes

## Discussion: from junior to senior

:::{.callout-note}
One minute with your project group, then three voices from the room:

If AI drafts most junior work, how does a junior analyst become a senior one?
:::

# [Send-off]{.flow} {.title}

## Keep programming

The skill fades if it sits idle. A few ways to keep it alive:

- Use Python in your **thesis**: data cleaning, analysis, plots you can defend
- Find a way to **apply it at work**: the repetitive task nobody wants to do by hand
- **[Advent of Code](https://adventofcode.com/)**: free, ad-free programming puzzles, one a day from **December 1st**. A genuinely fun way to keep the muscle warm.

## Thank you

- We covered the basics of Python: from a first `print` to a real project on your own machine
- I hope you enjoyed it, and I hope it's useful long after the grade
- If you have questions or feedback, [please tell me](mailto:vlcek@beyondsimulations.com)

. . .

All the best for your studies and your career. Now go build the thing.
